data.one_liner: A cache abstraction for wrapping in-memory or redis caches with timeouts.
data.what_it_does: It provides a unified caching abstraction layer that can wrap in-memory or Redis stores. It supports sub-caches using prefixes, custom codecs like UTF-8, timeouts, and automatic reconnects.
use_when: You need a consistent caching interface for Redis or in-memory stores.
You want to scope cached data using prefixes and apply custom data codecs.
avoid_when: You need local on-disk persistence like SQLite or Hive.
You require complex local key-value storage out of the box without setting up Redis.
strengths: Provides a clean abstraction over different cache providers like Redis.
Supports prefixes and codecs for easy data serialization and scoping.
weaknesses: Limited built-in provider options compared to larger caching libraries.
Testing Redis providers requires an external Redis instance.
data.setup_notes: Requires a running Redis instance if using the Redis cache provider.

alternatives.name: hive_ce
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you need a lightweight NoSQL key-value database stored locally on the device.

alternatives.name: shared_preferences
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you just need simple key-value storage for primitive types.
